text:
Bitcoin's marginal 1% decline to $63,400 reflects a broader flight to safety as renewed U.S. and Iranian strikes near the Strait of Hormuz drive global oil prices 4.5% higher. Despite this geopolitical friction and a "risk-off" transition across risk assets, the $2.26 trillion digital asset market maintains structural support. Regulatory momentum continues accelerating, with Circle securing a rare national trust bank charter and the European Union officially enforcing its MiCAR authorization framework.

Attention now pivots aggressively to the Federal Reserve and the upcoming June CPI data. With Chair Kevin Warsh establishing a strict data-dependent regime and ending traditional forward guidance, markets remain highly sensitive to any inflationary surprises. Sustained policy rates of 3.50%–3.75% continue to mechanically drain liquidity and elevate the opportunity cost of capital. Consequently, Bitcoin’s near-term trajectory remains tightly tethered to U.S. Treasury yields and dollar strength, as traditional equity headwinds spill directly into digital asset valuations.
